newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany says economic growth on track in Q2, H1.
newsitem.headline: Germany says economic growth on track in Q2, H1.

text.p: The German economy grew as much as one percent in the second quarter from the previous quarter and was up between 2.5 percent and 3.0 percent from a year ago, Econmics Minister Guenter Rexrodt said on Monday.

Rexrodt told reporters in Bonn that gross domestic product (GDP) expanded by around two percent in the first half of 1997 compared to a year ago, confirming that Germany is on track to match foreccasts of nearly 2.5 percent growth this year.
"The positive economic trend has accelerated thanks to booming exports and on the horizon the long-awaited turn in the labour market can be seen," Rexrodt said.

He said the government expects the economy to expand some 2.5 to 3.0 percent next year and that German exports, which have been fuelling economic recovery, will grow faster than world trade, increasing Germany's share of world markets.
Rexrodt said he saw no dangers to the economy from inflationary trends.
There would be an average 4.3 million people out of work in 1997, up 350,000 from the previous year, he said, adding that he expected a small decline in 1998.
All in all, Germany's economy was on track to allow it to qualify for European economic and monetary union.
"We will meet the criteria," he said.
